items.title: Woman Stabs 2, Killing One, in Times Square and Is Shot Dead by N.Y.P.D.
items.author: Andy Newman, Maria Cramer, Chelsia Rose Marcius and Caitlyn Freeman
items.content: <article>The police fired at the knife-wielding woman after trying to use less lethal force, officials said.</article>

items.title: Death Toll Rises in Grand Canyon Flood as Search Continues
items.author: Billy Witz and Thomas Fuller
items.content: <article>Officials announced a second death and said that more than a dozen people remain unaccounted for after heavy rain.</article>

items.title: Mansour Abbas Recruits Yoav Segalovitz to Join Raam Party in Israeli Election
items.author: David M. Halbfinger
items.content: <article>Mansour Abbas has recruited a Jewish lawmaker best known for reducing the crime rate in Arab cities. Could that be enough to get Mr. Abbas a seat in the next government?</article>

items.title: Supreme Court Allows White House Ballroom Construction to Continue
items.author: Matthew Cullen
items.content: <article>Also, a principal helped save 900 children in Nepal. Here’s the latest at the end of Monday.</article>

items.title: Nepal Puts Cost of Disaster at $5 Billion, Blaming Climate Change
items.author: Chico Harlan
items.content: <article>The country is seeking urgent help from a special U.N. climate fund, but the program lacks money because the United States and others have been reluctant to contribute.</article>

items.title: Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields: A New Feminist Music Festival Takes Shape
items.author: Lindsay Zoladz and Amanda Hakan
items.content: <article>At the first Daisy Chain Fields festival, the 23-year-old pop star presented a cross-generational vision of female empowerment. (With Taco Bell activations, too.)</article>

items.title: Study A.I. Consciousness? The Bots Would Like a Word With You.
items.author: Cade Metz
items.content: <article>Given access to email, A.I. agents have started reaching out to the philosophers and researchers exploring deep questions about them.</article>

items.title: What to Know About Hiking in Areas Prone to Flash Floods
items.author: Ryley Ober
items.content: <article>Canyons, small streams and dry creek beds in the West can be deceptively dangerous, trapping hikers when rainfall upstream causes rapidly rising water.</article>

items.title: Summit With Russia, India and Iran Shows Leverage Wars Have Given Xi of China
items.author: Paul Sonne and David Pierson
items.content: <article>A two-day conference of the 10-nation Shanghai Cooperation Organization in Kyrgyzstan shows the limits of U.S. economic warfare.</article>

items.title: DOJ Issues Grand Jury Subpoena to James Comey Confidant Daniel Richman
items.author: Alan Feuer
items.content: <article>The subpoena of Daniel C. Richman is the latest move in a persistent campaign to go after James B. Comey, one of President Trump’s most reviled political adversaries who has already been indicted twice.</article>

items.title: John Galliano Bows Out of Met Museum Show After Criticism Mounts
items.author: Vanessa Friedman and Jacob Bernstein
items.content: <article>Donors, politicians and Jewish leaders questioned the Met’s decision to honor Galliano, a fashion designer who was found guilty of a hate crime for his antisemitic outbursts.</article>

items.title: Democrats Have a Trump Card for Attacks On Wokeness
items.author: Frank Bruni
items.content: <article>The party that capitulated to Trump has the most to answer for</article>

items.title: A Principal Saved 900 Students Before His School Was Washed Away in Nepal
items.author: Binod Ghimire and Claire Moses
items.content: <article>Rajendra Dawadi had less than 15 minutes to act on a warning of approaching floodwaters. His swift evacuation plan saved hundreds of lives.</article>

items.title: What to Know About the Grand Canyon Flooding
items.author: Christine Hauser
items.content: <article>The bodies of at least two people were found and more than a dozen were missing. Further storms could hinder rescue efforts on Monday.</article>

items.title: Pennsylvania’s A.I. Gold Rush Meets Second Thoughts
items.author: David Gelles and Kristian Thacker
items.content: <article>Amid a backlash, Gov. Josh Shapiro is pumping the brakes on enormous data centers. But in a region scarred by the collapse of the steel industry, some welcome billions in construction.</article>

items.title: Senate Primary in Massachusetts Is a Generational Fight, With a Twist
items.author: Tim Balk
items.content: <article>In Massachusetts, the octogenarian senator Ed Markey faces a challenge from a much younger centrist, Representative Seth Moulton.</article>

items.title: These Generals Fought for Israel. Now They See ‘Jewish Terrorism’ as the Threat.
items.author: Azam Ahmed, Natan Odenheimer, Ronen Bergman and Ivor Prickett
items.content: <article>A growing number of former Israeli generals, intelligence officials and prime ministers are accusing settlers in the West Bank of committing ethnic cleansing with government support. “Once a society behaves this way,” one said, “that society is doomed.”</article>

items.title: ‘Hey! You’re the Jerk at the Beach!’
items.author: Thomas Beller
items.content: <article>As New Yorkers, we’re used to negotiating over tiny patches of space. But I didn’t expect that to continue on the beach.</article>
